test_cases.title: Case-insensitive multi-role token resolves deterministically to architect regardless of array order
test_cases.given: a decoded bearer token's realm_access.roles = ['Architect', 'Developer', 'developer'] (the live 2026-09-10 case)
test_cases.when: CurrentUser is constructed and persona_resolver.resolve is invoked via GET /api/me
test_cases.then: persona resolves deterministically to 'architect' on every call, regardless of the roles' order in the token array, per default precedence cio > architect > product-manager > engineering-manager > developer
test_cases.objective: Verify that a multi-role token containing case-variant and duplicate role claims resolves deterministically to the correct persona per the configured precedence order, independent of the roles' array order in the token, reproducing the live 2026-09-10 regression.
preconditions: Persona resolver Tier-2 YAML (services/api/config/persona_role_map.yaml) carries the shipped mapping architect: architect and developer: developer, casefolded at load time per AUTH-07-FR-7.

No Tier-1 PERSONA_PRECEDENCE_ORDER env var or Tier-2 precedence: override is set for this test — resolver falls back to the hardcoded default order ["cio", "architect", "product-manager", "engineering-manager", "developer"] per AUTH-07-FR-6.
A valid bearer token is issued (via /auth/dev-bypass or a signed test JWT) with realm_access.roles set per test_data.
Persona resolver's 300s per-role cache is cold at test start (fresh resolver instance or cache explicitly cleared) so the resolution path actually executes rather than serving a stale cached value.
steps: Issue a bearer token whose decoded realm_access.roles equals roles_order_a.
Call GET /api/me with the token in the Authorization: Bearer header; record the returned persona.
Repeat step 1-2 with roles_order_b in a fresh token/session (same underlying role set, different array order).
Compare the persona value returned across all three calls.
expected_results: All three calls return 200 {"name": ..., "persona": "architect"} — the response body's persona field equals expected_persona in every case.
The resolved persona does not vary with the token array's role order, confirming precedence-driven (not positional) selection.
current_user.role (the precedence-selected winner passed to persona_resolver.resolve) equals architect for all three token variants.
No PersonaResolutionError (ambiguous_case_collision) is raised, since Architect/architect differ only across the token's role list, not within a single config tier's key set.

test_cases.title: All-tiers-miss role emits distinguishable persona_mapping_not_found event and still raises PersonaNotFoundError
test_cases.given: every surviving role on a token fails to resolve in any of the 3 tiers, after casefolding
test_cases.when: persona_resolver.resolve is attempted for that role
test_cases.then: PersonaNotFoundError is raised (fail-closed unchanged) AND a persona_mapping_not_found log event fires carrying the attempted role(s) and tiers consulted, with no user_id/email/name/groups, distinguishable from persona_mapping_loaded and rbac_check_org_access outcome=denied
test_cases.objective: Verify an all-tiers-miss role emits a grep-distinguishable persona_mapping_not_found log event (correct fields, no PII) and still fails closed with PersonaNotFoundError — using a handler attached directly to the resolver's own logger so the assertion cannot pass vacuously under Alembic's fileConfig logger sweep.
preconditions: A _RecordCapturingHandler (per the existing precedent in services/api/tests/unit/test_persona_resolver.py) is instantiated and attached directly to the app.core.persona_resolver logger — the logger is force-enabled (logger.disabled = False, logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)) and de-propagated (logger.propagate = False) BEFORE the resolve call, because Alembic's fileConfig(disable_existing_loggers=True) disables every app.* logger process-wide and a caplog/capsys-based assertion would pass vacuously after any migrated_db test.

Tier-1 (PERSONA_ROLE_MAP / PERSONA_PRECEDENCE_ORDER), Tier-2 YAML, and Tier-3 persona_config / persona_precedence are all confirmed to hold no entry, under any casefolding, for the test role nonexistent-role.
Resolver's per-role cache is cold for nonexistent-role (fresh instance or cache cleared) so the miss actually traverses all 3 tiers rather than serving a cached result.
steps: Attach the _RecordCapturingHandler directly to the app.core.persona_resolver logger; force-enable and de-propagate it.
Call persona_resolver.resolve("nonexistent-role") directly (or via GET /api/me with a token whose sole surviving role is nonexistent-role).
Capture the raised exception and the handler's captured log records.
Inspect the captured records for an event named persona_mapping_not_found and its extra fields.
Inspect the same captured records to confirm no persona_mapping_loaded or rbac_check_org_access event was emitted for this call, and that no captured record carries user_id/email/name/groups.
expected_results: persona_resolver.resolve("nonexistent-role") raises PersonaNotFoundError (fail-closed unchanged); if invoked via GET /api/me, the endpoint returns 403.
Exactly one persona_mapping_not_found log record is captured, with extra["roles"] containing nonexistent-role and extra["tiers_consulted"] equal to expected_tiers_consulted in that order.
The captured persona_mapping_not_found record carries no user_id, email, name, or groups field.

No persona_mapping_loaded event is present in the captured records for this call, and no rbac_check_org_access outcome=denied event is present either — the event name alone is sufficient to distinguish an unmapped role from a matched-but-RBAC-denied role.
